newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW - Orion sees more Hygicult sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Orion sees more Hygicult sales.

text.p: Tighter hygiene control laws in the EU and U.S. will increase demand for Finnish pharmaceuticals group Orion-yhtyma Oy's hygiene control product range Hygicult, Orion Diagnostica's president Matti Vaheri said.
In an interview with Reuters on Wednesday, Vaheri said the new laws would start coming into force next year, helping the group boost sales of the over ten-year-old product range.
"Sales of this product will certainly increase manifold," Vaheri said.

Vaheri said Hygicult products are "significant" for his division which accounted for 201 million markka or five percent of Orion's 1995 net sales but he declined to give the products' current sales figures.
Hygicult products help find general bacteria, yeasts and fungi in various environments and Vaheri said they are the leading dip-slide products of their kind.
Vaheri said growth in Hygicult sales could help Diagnostica's profits in 1997. The division in 1995 posted a 17 million markka operating profit, down from 22 million in 1994.
"Already next year the growth of this market will be seen to some extent (in profits and turnover)," he said.

The market for Hygicult, currently mainly used in hospitals, is expected to grow rapidly in Europe and in U.S. since planned legislation expands demand for high-quality hygiene control to the food industry and to all food processing, including restaurants and trade, Vaheri said.
"In Europe, the market for this sector is expected to be $1.2 to $1.6 billion by 2000, which is five or ten fold compared to the current market," he said.
In the U.S., tighter hygiene control will take effect gradually starting in 1997 in the meat processing industry, Vaheri said.

U.S. hygiene control equipment maker Neogen said earlier it would start marketing Orion's Hygicult products range to the U.S. food industry and Vaheri said Orion will start marketing Neogen's hygiene control products in Europe.
"Neogen may be a good partner for us in hygiene control as it has specialised in that sector," he added.
